purpose: Compare Pulse's detector with standard unsupervised baselines on identical data, identical conformal thresholding, identical k-of-n confirmation and matched alert budgets; only the scorer differs.
reference_arm: base29 = Pulse scorer (ExtraTrees history->current + support branch, joint p-value), the syscall-arms base29 models

baseline_arms.iforest: Isolation Forest (200 trees) on the standardized current 249-column vector; score = -score_samples
baseline_arms.autoencoder: MLP autoencoder (249-64-16-64-249) reconstructing the standardized current vector; score = mean squared reconstruction error (frequency autoencoder in the spirit of CDL)
baseline_arms.freq_profile: Bag-of-system-calls style frequency deviation: L1 distance of the syscall-frequency part (29 ratios + 64 hashed syscall bins) to the training mean, scaled by training MAD

fit_data: syscall-arms normal selection rows, same train/calibration split and capped indices as Pulse's syscall-arms fits (train contexts, current vector)

evaluation_data.normal: pulse-live-recalibrated normal 19/10 13:00 - capture end, incident 18:25-19:20 removed; first 42 % (to ~18:25) used as calibration, the rest for alert burden
evaluation_data.attacks: pulse-live-recalibrated main + follow-up campaigns (420 pairs: idle control, benign launch, attack)

decision: joint p-value of each scorer (baselines put the same score in both branches), k2of2 confirmation, alpha scale matched per arm to the budget
statistics: paired workload-clustered bootstrap (10000) of differences to base29
reported_as: base29 better / not different / worse per baseline, using 95 % CIs of the recall and separation differences at each budget; no selection of a winner after the fact
evidence_class: development: the evaluation run is the same capture used elsewhere for selection; attack scenarios were used while developing Pulse
